title: 4 paranormal romances to read this Halloween season
byline: Jackie Varriano from The Seattle Times
excerpt: For your reading this season, instead of bloodcurdling screams or scary stories, here's a roundup of heartwarming romances with a paranormal twist.
content:
All Hallows’ Eve is almost upon us, but there's still time for ghosts, witches, reapers and all things paranormal. 

And for your reading pleasure, instead of bloodcurdling screams or scary stories, here's a roundup of heartwarming romances with a paranormal twist. Think grim reapers who are tired of death and the drudgery of ferrying souls, star-crossed lovers thrown together through time portals and witches who must fake date to solve a mystery.

“Grim Tidings” by B.K. Borison (out now from Avon). Darcy has been a grim reaper since her death in 1918, and the repetitiveness of being with people on the worst days of their lives has started to take its toll. 

After her latest assignment lands her in a small, coastal New England town, she decides to throw out the rule book and attempt to save someone instead of leading them to the afterlife. The only person standing in her way is the hot, tattooed bar owner Gabriel, who also happens to be a guardian angel. Drawn to each other like magnets, the two clash over what's right, what's wrong and what’s going to happen next. 

This is Borison’s second paranormal romance novel — set in the same universe as 2025’s “Good Spirits” — and it’s chock full of similar swoony yearning and emotional payoff, with a hint of a third book in the “Ghosted” series to come.

“Written in Starlight” by Sloane Brooks (out now from Atria Books). Fans of Erin Morgenstern’s “The Starless Sea” or Lev Grossman’s “The Magicians” will love the meddlesome librarians in “Written in Starlight.”

Set in a world where every person’s life is detailed in a series of books, “Written in Starlight” tells the story of Della, an earthbound maid, and Ansel, an intergalactic outlaw, who find each other’s books and discover they can write to one another through them. As Della and Ansel decide to see just how far they can push the magic, a portal romance across space and time unfolds. 

There’s a whole host of funny alien side characters and good comic relief when Della’s Victorian-era world collides with Ansel’s spaceship after she writes herself into his book. They soon realize that every intervention has a price, and they’ll have to work extra hard to best the librarians and get the ending of their dreams.  

“Love You to Death” by Jenna Levine (out now from Berkley). Daniel is a beleaguered reaper, burnt out after decades of collecting souls for the Agency, a workplace that proves corporate life is a paperwork-filled drag no matter where you are.

Imagine his surprise when Lucy McKenzie willingly touches his arm — the first contact he’s had in ages — and shows him the brightest soul he’s seen in forever. Unfortunately, he’s there to take her to the afterlife. When she pleads for her life (she’s got things to do, after all!), Daniel breaks protocol and convinces the higher-ups to give Lucy six more weeks of life in exchange for Daniel’s observations on humanity.

What follows is an exploration of all the most beautiful, messy human experiences and the realization that true love might be the thing that brings them both back to life.

“Vengefully Matched” by Audrey Goldberg Ruoff (out now from Atria Books). Looking for an age gap, fake dating, witchy, sapphic romance? This book has it all. 

Meet Priscilla Hart, a runaway bride and a member of the Witchery Council looking to rehab her reputation after leaving her bride (and former Witchery Council president) in the dust at the altar. First order of business? Prank her new nemesis, Agatha Vanderbilt Voisin, the newly elected council president and a blond, bubbly, pink-loving foil to Priscilla’s moody goth girl persona. However, when a series of magical explosions leave prank-loving Priscilla as the main suspect, Agatha decides to trust Priscilla and — in order to save her from an inquisition — announces they're dating.

The two (each harboring a secret crush) use their fake relationship as a cover to team up and find out who is wreaking havoc in the magical town of Hallowcross. It’s not long before those fake feelings turn very real in this steamy book set in the same universe as Goldbery Ruoff’s 2025 release “Hopelessly Teavoted.”
